body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36338

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2687

## What changed

- Selectively dequantize the union of physical FP8 KV slots used by ragged BF16 DSA sparse prefill.
- Translate logical top-k positions through the flattened page table before deduplication, so shared-prefix physical aliases are staged only once.
- Remap top-k indices to the compact BF16 buffer while preserving `-1`/invalid entries and the all-invalid sentinel-row contract.
- Retain full-prefix dequantization below a conservative 131,072-row floor or when the unique union does not save enough work.
- Add GPU numerical, compatibility, aliasing, fallback, and adversarial tests plus a reproducible staging-path benchmark.

## Reproduce

```bash
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-f631daba9e47/cache/triton
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-f631daba9e47/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_selective_dsa_kv_dequant.py -s
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-f631daba9e47/venv/bin/python \
  reports/j-f631daba9e47/benchmark_selective_dequant.py
```

On the assigned MI350X, the focused tests pass (3 passed). At 262,144 logical rows with 8 query rows and top-k 2,048, the physical union was 4,029 rows. BF16 staging fell from 301,989,888 to 4,641,408 bytes, and the measured full/selective times were 0.7931/0.3013 ms (2.632x).

All scoped pre-commit checks pass. No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.

## Limitations

- `flashmla_sparse` BF16 attention is NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell-only. The assigned AMD MI350X validated the real Triton dequantization plus remapping numerically, but could not execute the final FlashMLA attention kernel. This is therefore reported as `candidate_verified`, not a fully target-architecture-qualified fix.
- The repository's real FP8 DSA prefill fixture stops before attention on this HIP setup because its page size is 64 while the prepared legacy HIP DSA path requires page size 1. The raw traceback and exact command are recorded under `reports/j-f631daba9e47/`.
- The 131,072-row floor is deliberately conservative and measured on MI350X. It is not claimed as an independently calibrated NVIDIA or end-to-end model threshold.
- No architecture-matching full-model weights were available; a serving startup smoke would not validate this kernel feature and was not substituted.

Detailed claims and remaining limitations are in `reports/j-f631daba9e47/result.json`.
